text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"states a clear opposition and repeats reasons throughout","quality":"stance clarity","description":"It makes the writer’s position unmistakable and keeps returning to that position as the essay develops."},{"evidence":"asks what happens if the technology fails and who is at fault","quality":"reasoning depth","description":"It goes beyond simple opinion by exploring consequences and accountability if driverless systems break down."},{"evidence":"mentions lane changes, potholes, stop signs, and a child crossing","quality":"specific support","description":"It uses concrete driving situations to make the safety argument more vivid and convincing."},{"evidence":"asks a concluding choice between safety and looking cool","quality":"persuasive closing","description":"It ends by directly challenging the reader and reinforcing the main argument in a memorable way."},{"evidence":"several paragraphs built around separate concerns","quality":"organization","description":"It separates ideas into distinct points, which makes the argument easier to follow."}]}
